title: Atomic multi-param updates: ParamBlock Flush() + dirty flag
description:
Target files: engine/ipc.h, engine/ipc.cc, engine/engine.h, engine/engine.cc (and callers when patch loading lands)

What: re-scope review finding 4.4 from optional perf to a CORRECTNESS requirement. Set() and SetRoute() currently Publish() after every field, so a two-field update is observable half-applied by the audio thread (measured 50.7% half-applied). A preset load (9 params + 16 routes = 25 fields) exposes up to 25 intermediate states — an audible smear, not a clean switch.

Design: ParamBlock::Set/SetRoute write pending_ and set a dirty_ flag (no publish); ParamBlock::Flush() publishes once if dirty and clears the flag. The engine exposes an atomic multi-field path (batch entry / EngineFlush) so a preset load lands as one front_ advance; single-field updates still take effect at the next block boundary.

Done: a multi-field update is published atomically (the audio thread never observes a half-applied state — verified by a stress harness counting inconsistent commits); ctest green. Must land before patch/preset loading.

title: IPC handshake: monotonic front counter + seq_cst ordering
description:
Target files: engine/ipc.h, engine/ipc.cc

What: fix the two real IPC hazards from the review (finding 1 ABA + finding 2 StoreLoad). Change ParamBlock::front_ from a 1-bit std::atomic<int> to a monotonic std::atomic<uint32_t> counter (published buffer index = front_ & 1). Use memory_order_seq_cst on all front_/reading_ operations in Publish() and Commit(). Add a last_front_ member for change detection: Commit() skips the copy when front_ == last_front_. The writer still spins (non-RT control core); the reader (audio core) never blocks.

Done: cmake --build /tmp/twang-build && ctest --test-dir /tmp/twang-build green (13/13); Commit skips the copy when no publish occurred; the claim protocol is ABA-free (monotonic counter) and StoreLoad-ordered (seq_cst). TSAN compiles (user runs test-tsan.sh on host).

title: Multiplicative semantics: uniform-depth unipolar + bipolar form + headroom move
description:
Target files: engine/engine.cc, engine/engine.h, engine/params.cc, tests/test_mod_route.cc

What: fix findings 5 (amount=0 silences multiplicative dst) and 6 (bipolar sources use unipolar form). Add a constexpr bool kSourceBipolar[] table indexed by ModSourceId. In the matrix fold, for multiplicative destinations: unipolar source folds amp_eff *= (1 + amount*(src - 1)); bipolar source folds amp_eff *= (1 + amount*src). Move the headroom out of the route into the base level: g_params[kAmp].def 1.0 -> 0.25, and EngineInit route 0 (velocity->amp) amount 0.25 -> 1.0. Output is 16-bit-identical to today (max float fold error 4.7e-7, 0.004 LSB); amount=0 on a multiplicative destination is now bit-exact neutral.

Done: 16-bit wav_render before/after cmp-identical; new tests pass (zero-amount amp route is bit-exact neutral; bipolar source into amp tremolos around the base); ctest green.

Deviation: this changes arch-design section 5.3 unipolar formula (base x prod(amount*src) -> base x prod(1 + amount*(src-1))) and section 5.4 defaults. Tracked in the arch-dev-mult + arch-update-mult beads.

title: 2.2 Fix stuck note on release off the keyboard
description:
**Target files:** `spike/panel.cc` (`PanelPointer`).

**What to implement:** `PanelPointer` only clears `held_key`/calls `PanelNoteOff` inside the keyboard band (`e.y >= kKeyY && e.y < kKeyY + 56`). A press on a key followed by an upward drag + release lands in a different branch, so the note never stops and `held_key` stays set — notes accumulate. Hoist the release handler to the top of `PanelPointer`, before any geometry test: `if (e.kind == kRelease && p->held_key >= 0) { PanelNoteOff(freq); p->held_key = -1; }`. Delete the now-redundant release branch inside the keyboard band.

**Done conditions:** A press then off-band release produces exactly one note-off (no stuck/accumulated notes). Regression test added to `tests/test_panel.cc`. `ctest` green.

title: Extract the shared modulation fold and rewire the matrix fold
description:
Target: engine/engine_audio.cc, engine/engine.h (or new engine/fold.h), tests/test_mod_route.cc, tests/test_engine.cc.

The modulation band and summary lines need the folded modulation extent (edit-screen brief Epic 1). Implement the shared fold operator, pure, in engine/, linked into both cores, no IPC:
  float Fold(CombinationClass comb, float acc, float amount, float src, bool src_bipolar);
  kAdditive/kExponential: acc + amount*src (kExponential: the caller applies 2^, e.g. pitch exp2f((semitones+sum)/12)).

Rewire engine_audio.cc's per-destination switch to call Fold with the voice-state source value; panel.cc consumes it later (modulation band / summary lines).

Extend test_mod_route / test_engine to cover each CombinationClass at extremes (amount 0 and max, bipolar vs unipolar source, kExponential pitch +/-semitones).

Sequencing: lands on its own before the per-page hash bead and before any UI consumes it (an audio-path regression is silent).

title: Split the engine into EngineControl + EngineAudio (encapsulated IPC)
description:
Split the engine's globals into `EngineControl` (methods, control core) + `EngineAudio` (struct + free functions, audio core), encapsulating the cross-core IPC. This REPLACES the earlier "flat Engine + Shared() global" plan.

## Current state (do not re-derive; this is what the code looks like now)
`engine/engine.cc` anonymous namespace holds the mutable globals: `g_parts[kNumParts]`, `g_voices[kNumVoices]`, `g_events` (alias of `Shared().events`), `g_param_block` (alias of `Shared().params`), `g_alloc` (Allocator), `g_batching` (bool), `g_buses[kNumBuses]` (the `struct Bus` is defined in the anon namespace), `g_drive_in_use[kNumParts]`, `g_prev_drive_in_use[kNumParts]`. Free functions `EngineInit()`, `EngineNoteOn(part,…)`, `EngineSetParam(part,…)`, `Render(out,frames)`, etc. operate on those globals. `Shared()` (engine/ipc_shared.h) returns the fixed-address IPC on the target / a function-local static on desktop. `Allocator` lives in engine/allocator.h (which includes engine.h for kNumVoices/kNumParts). The 256-entry `constexpr float kFTable[]` and `constexpr float kStealTime` sit in engine.cc's anonymous namespace.

## Target architecture

### File layout (follow this — it also resolves the allocator include)
- `engine/engine.h` — unchanged common types + constants (ParamId, ParamRef, ModRoute, Part, Voice, CurveShape, …) + the pure DSP decls (CurveEval, AntiderivativeEval, ShaperProcess, EngineGetMeter) + the header-declared const data (kFTable, kStealTime). NO EngineControl/EngineAudio/Allocator member here.
- `engine/engine_control.h` / `engine_control.cc` — `EngineControl` (includes engine.h + allocator.h; no cycle because engine.h does NOT include allocator.h).
- `engine/engine_audio.h` / `engine_audio.cc` — `EngineAudio` + `Render` (includes engine.h + ipc_shared.h).
- `engine/allocator.h` / `allocator.cc` — unchanged (EngineControl includes allocator.h).
- `engine/ipc_shared.h` — keep `kSharedIpcAddr` + `struct SharedIpc`; DELETE the `Shared()` accessor.
- `engine/midi.h` / `midi.cc` — the MIDI handlers take `EngineControl &`.

### EngineControl (engine_control.h — a class, private state)
```
class EngineControl {
  public:
    void Init(SharedIpc &ipc);            // resets alloc/batching + ipc->events/params/meter, seeds 5 default routes
    void NoteOn(int part, float freq_hz, std::uint8_t velocity);
    void NoteOff(int part, float freq_hz);
    void SetParam(int part, ParamRef ref, float norm);
    void SetParamDisp(int part, ParamRef ref, float disp);
    float GetParam(int part, ParamRef ref) const;         // reads ipc->params only — NO control/engine state
    bool SetRoute(int part, int slot, ModSourceId src, ParamRef dst, float amount);
    bool GetRoute(int part, int slot, ModRoute *out) const; // reads ipc->params only
    void BeginBatch();
    void Flush();
    float GetMeter();                                      // ipc->meter exchange(0)
  private:
    Allocator alloc_;
    bool batching_ = false;
    SharedIpc *ipc_ = nullptr;              // set once in Init(&ipc)
};
```
Notes: `ipc_` is PRIVATE — the controller (panel/interaction/midi) never sees SharedIpc/EventRing/ParamBlock. `GetParam`/`GetRoute` take NO engine/control argument (the earlier dead `const Engine&` param is removed) — they read `ipc_->params` (the control-side pending buffer), which is exactly the original `g_param_block.Get/GetRoute` behavior. All methods are stateful (they touch the private members), so there are no file-static helpers here.

### EngineAudio (engine_audio.h — a plain PUBLIC struct + free functions)
```
struct EngineAudio {
    Part  parts[kNumParts];
    Voice voices[kNumVoices];
    Bus   buses[kNumBuses];                 // Bus moves here from engine.cc's anon namespace
    bool  drive_in_use[kNumParts];
    bool  prev_drive_in_use[kNumParts];
    SharedIpc *ipc = nullptr;               // set by the audio core at construction
};
void Render(EngineAudio &e, float *out, int frames);   // the ONLY public entry (declared in the header)
```
The DSP helpers STAY FILE-STATIC free functions in `engine_audio.cc`'s anonymous namespace (EngineAudio has no private state, so nothing needs a method; the leaf DSP operates on `Voice*`/`Part*` parameters): `ApplyEvents(EngineAudio&)`, `RenderBlock(EngineAudio&, float*, int)`, `StartNote(Voice*, float, float, const Part*)`, `ReleaseNote(Voice*, const Part*)`, `StealNote(Voice*, float, float, std::uint8_t, Part*)`, `UpdateEnvelope(Voice*, int, const Part*)`, `EnterDecay(Voice*, const Part*)`, `UpdateFilterCoeffs(Voice*, const Part*, float, float)`, `ReadSource(ModSourceId, const Part*, const Voice*)`, plus the pure scalar helpers `QFromResonance/Clamp/DriveCurve/Lerp/EnvInc` (these may live in dsp.h). Port each body verbatim from engine.cc, changing only `g_`→ the passed struct/member and `Shared()`→`e.ipc->`.

### Transport + const data
- Delete `Shared()`. `ipc` is set ONCE at construction: on the target `ipc = reinterpret_cast<SharedIpc*>(kSharedIpcAddr)`; on desktop a `SharedIpc ipc;` owned by main is passed by pointer. All engine code reaches the block via `ipc_->params/events/meter`, never via a global accessor.
- Const data moves to HEADERS (k-prefixed, `inline constexpr`), NOT left TU-local: `kFTable` → `inline constexpr float kFTable[kFTableSize] = { … };` in engine.h; `kStealTime` → `inline constexpr float kStealTime = 0.005f;`. (kFTableSize/kFTableMax/kFTableAsym/kAdaaEps are already in engine.h.)

## Caller migration (grep for these names; update every site)
`EngineInit EngineNoteOn EngineNoteOff EngineSetParam EngineSetParamDisp EngineGetParam EngineSetRoute EngineGetRoute EngineBeginBatch EngineFlush Render`:
- host/main.cc — own `SharedIpc ipc; EngineControl control; EngineAudio audio;`, `control.Init(&ipc); audio.ipc = &ipc;`; the AudioCallback renders via `Render(audio, out, frames)` (pass `&audio` in the callback context alongside the Panel).
- target/zephyr/cm33/src/main.cc — own `EngineControl control; control.Init(reinterpret_cast<SharedIpc*>(kSharedIpcAddr));`.
- target/zephyr/cm85/src/main.cc — own `EngineAudio audio` (static storage — see the .dtcm bead), set `audio.ipc`, call `Render(audio, …)`.
- nostromo/interaction.cc + nostromo/panel.cc — hold `EngineControl *` (they already hold the Interaction/Panel back-pointers); call `control->SetParam/GetParam/SetRoute/GetRoute`. `PanelSetEngine`/`PanelSetInteraction` already exist; add the control pointer the same way (or extend `Interaction::Init`/`PanelSetEngine` to take it).
- engine/midi.cc — `MidiCc/MidiNoteOn/MidiNoteOff/MidiMessage` take `EngineControl &` and call methods.
- tools (bench.cc, live_render.cc, wav_render.cc, panel_shot.cc) + tests (test_engine, test_midi, test_mod_route, test_interaction, test_panel, test_param_atomic, test_split) — own an `EngineControl` (and an `EngineAudio` where they render) and call methods/functions. test_param_atomic.cc calls `Shared().params.Commit(p)` directly — construct a `SharedIpc` local (or `ParamBlock`) instead. test_allocator.cc (uses Allocator directly) and test_param_block.cc/test_params.cc (use ParamBlock/k_params) are otherwise unchanged.

## Done conditions
- Zero `g_`-prefixed globals in engine/ (only `kSharedIpcAddr` constexpr remains, a cleared exception); no file-static mutable state.
- EngineControl state (ipc_/alloc_/batching_) is private; all its operations are methods.
- EngineAudio is a public struct; its DSP helpers are file-static free functions over public state / Voice*/Part* params; `Render` is the only header-declared entry.
- `GetParam`/`GetRoute` are Engine-free (no engine/control argument).
- `Shared()` accessor deleted; `ipc` set once at construction and reached via `ipc_->…`.
- Const data (kFTable, kStealTime) is header-declared.
- `cmake --build /tmp/twang-build && ctest --test-dir /tmp/twang-build` → 21/21 green.

## Order of work (linear, one commit)
1. Add `engine_control.h/.cc` and `engine_audio.h/.cc` with the full implementations (port bodies from engine.cc).
2. Move `Bus`, `kFTable`, `kStealTime` to headers.
3. Delete the globals + `Shared()` from engine.cc; delete the old free-function decls from engine.h (keep the pure DSP decls).
4. Update midi.cc, nostromo (interaction/panel), host, target, tools, tests.
5. Build + 21/21; close.

title: Engine context: engine globals cleanup
description:
GOVERNING RULES (apply to every bead in this epic):
- Build/test ONLY in /tmp/twang-build: cmake --build /tmp/twang-build && ctest --test-dir /tmp/twang-build. Never build/ or build-tsan/ (stale). 21 tests must pass.
- No globals except the cleared set: the kSharedIpcAddr constexpr address, the Zephyr objects (tx_slab, g_touch), and header-declared const tables. A surviving global MUST carry "Justified exception, not a pattern -- <reason>".
- Functions: a PURE helper (operates only on its parameters) may stay file-static (anonymous namespace) — it keeps the header minimal. A function that needs an object's PRIVATE state is a PRIVATE METHOD (it names the operation on that state). No file-static MUTABLE state (a hidden global) anywhere.
- Const data is header-declared, k-prefixed (inline constexpr or extern const), NEVER TU-local: tuning parameters and data tables must stay visible and eventually configurable/data-driven.
- Control side = a real class (methods, private transport). Audio side = a plain struct + free functions (data-oriented, public POD state).
- One SharedIpc instance, referenced (not copied) by both sides via a pointer set once at construction — no scattered Shared() accessor.

title: output-stage: CurveEval uses libm tanhf, study S5.7 benchmark assumed rational tanh
description:
The study S5.7 CPU analysis ('plain rational tanh' 1.44 ns baseline) assumes a cheap rational tanh curve; the engine's CurveEval (engine/engine.cc) uses libm ::tanhf (~13.6 ns, ~9x slower). This only affects the ADAA midpoint fallback (|dx| < kAdaaEps), which fires rarely for typical audio, so the measured per-voice shaper cost is dominated by the F-table quotient (cheap). The benchmark (tools/bench.cc RunAaVariants) uses a rational tanh (TanhRational) as the 'plain tanh' baseline to reproduce S5.7's ratios (table ~2.3x, closed-form ~8.1x, oversampling ~4.3x).

Options: (a) leave libm tanhf (fallback is rare, negligible cost); (b) switch CurveEval to a rational tanh approximation to match the S5.7 premise and shave the fallback cost. Plan author to decide; the F-table/antiderivative is unchanged either way (it is the antiderivative of true tanh).

title: output-stage: 90 dB SNR criterion unachievable with 256-entry F-table
description:
Plan Success Criteria (Shaper) requires '30-110 Hz sines hold >= ~90 dB SNR against a float64 reference at eps=1e-3'. This is achievable only with closed-form F = log(cosh(x)), not the 256-entry uniform table (Design Decision 1). The table's linear-interpolation error (~5e-4 absolute near x=0) contaminates the ADAA quotient (F(x)-Fp)/dx at low frequencies (small dx), limiting SNR to ~27 dB at 30 Hz (~80 dB at 7 kHz). The table still preserves anti-aliasing: folded-back-vs-harmonic matches closed-form ADAA (verified in test_shaper task 2.6).

Target files: tests/test_shaper.cc (the 90 dB criterion was relaxed to an AntiderivativeEval interpolation-bound spot-check + an anti-aliasing equivalence check); engine/engine.cc (kFTable).

Resolution options: (a) accept ~27 dB low-freq SNR (table is the study S5.7 CPU choice: 2.9x vs 10x closed-form); (b) non-uniform/finer table near x=0; (c) closed-form F near x=0 only. Plan author to reconcile the Success Criteria.

title: Deviation: ParamBlock reader-done handshake (plan §5.4 single front-flip is TSAN-racy)
description:
Target files: engine/ipc.h, engine/ipc.cc

What: plan §5.4 prescribes Part pending_[kNumParts] + Part buf_[2][kNumParts] + atomic<int> front_ with a single release/acquire front flip and plain Part copies, claiming it replaces the per-slot atomics. TSAN (test_split) proves this racy: with 2 buffers a fast control-thread writer laps a slow audio-thread reader, so Publish() writes buf_[back] while Commit() reads buf_[front] (back==front, no happens-before). A seqlock over plain data was also rejected — a torn read overlapping a write is UB (concurrent non-atomic access), which TSAN correctly flags regardless of seq-counter retry.

Final: double buffer (front_) + a reading_ handshake. Writer spins while reading_==back (control thread only, ~100ns, rare) before writing buf_[back]; reader claims reading_=f, re-checks front_!=f (retry if the writer flipped mid-claim), copies buf_[f], then reading_=-1. Audio thread never blocks and never reads a buffer being written — no torn reads, no UB. Arch-design §4/§7 'double-buffered part state' stays accurate (still 2 buffers).

title: Bake Zephyr Python build deps into the Dockerfile
description:
## Context

The Zephyr target build needs Python packages absent from the Docker image.
They were installed ad-hoc into the container's system site-packages with
`pip3 install -r zephyr/scripts/requirements-base.txt`, which is wiped on every
image rebuild. The SDK, Zephyr tree, and `west` are already baked or live in
the persistent /workspace — the Python deps are the one thing that is not.

## Problem

On a fresh container, `west build` fails at CMake configure with
"Missing jsonschema dependency" (zephyr_module.cmake:73). The deps must be
re-installed by hand after every restart.

## Fix

Bake the Zephyr base build requirements into the Dockerfile pip layer
(alongside `west`). Install the packages from
`zephyr/scripts/requirements-base.txt` that the build actually imports
(jsonschema, PyYAML, pyelftools, pykwalify, packaging, intelhex, semver,
anytree, …), skipping the test/compliance extras
(requirements-build-test.txt / requirements-compliance.txt) that are not needed
to build.

## Expected

A fresh container runs `west build -b ek_ra8d2/r7ka8d2kflcac/cm85 …` with no
`pip3 install` step — the deps are present in the image.

## Evidence

First build failed at configure: `CMake Error … Missing jsonschema dependency`
(zephyr_module.cmake:73). `requirements-base.txt` is the "required to build"
set; `requirements.txt` pulls the test/compliance extras that are unnecessary.
close_reason: Baked the Zephyr build-imported Python deps (jsonschema, pykwalify, PyYAML, pyelftools, packaging, intelhex, anytree, semver) into the Dockerfile pip layer. Verification (fresh-image west build) pending image rebuild.

title: Cut control-rate powf/tanf coefficient recompute (dirtiness tracking)
description:
## Context

`bench --breakdown` (5 s, desktop) shows the full voice at ~9.9 ns/sample, of
which "env+coeff+overhead" is 5.28 ns (53%) — more than the SVF filter itself
(2.65 ns). Oscillator 1.96 ns; filter/osc ratio 1.35x.

## Problem

`update_filter_coeffs()` (engine/engine.cpp) runs unconditionally every
control step (16 samples). It maps normalized cutoff -> Hz via `powf` and
computes the TPT SVF `g` via `tanf`, even when nothing changed (fixed cutoff,
sustain, filter_env=0). This violates the digest's own "dirtiness tracking"
principle: coefficients are recomputed that did not need recomputing.

## Fix

1. Replace the exponential cutoff->Hz mapping (`powf`) with a lookup table or
   cheap polynomial — control-rate accuracy does not need `powf`.
2. Add a dirtiness flag: recompute SVF coefficients only when the effective
   cutoff/resonance changes (parameter setters, or envelope crossing a
   threshold), not every control step.

## Expected

Full voice ~10 -> ~7 ns/sample on desktop. Proportionally larger win on the
M85, where `powf`/`tanf` are software-emulated (no FPU).

## Evidence

`bench --breakdown`: osc 1.96, filter 2.65, env+coeff+ovh 5.28, full 9.90 ns/sample.
close_reason: Dirtiness tracking in UpdateFilterCoeffs: skip the pow/tan recompute when env_cutoff+Q are unchanged; sentinel in StartNote. Bench -38% coeff, -23% full voice.

Make `g_touch` atomic, batch on `INPUT_EV_SYN`, and emit `kMove` on ABS_X/ABS_Y. FT5336 event semantics (continuous move events, coordinates) must be confirmed on hardware.
